newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice price falls this week in listess market.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice price falls this week in listess market.

text.p: Thai rice prices eased slightly from the previous week on sluggish demand, trade sources said on Thursday.
The Thai benchmark 100 percent white B rice for September/October shipment was quoted at around US$340 per tonne FOB Bangkok, compared with $345-355 last week.
Traders said they heard of few new enquiries this week.
Buying interest waned as exporters said they had bought enough rice to cover their demand. Many were sidelined waiting for the new crop to enter the market in November.
Buying was also low because of slow traffic and fewer ships had arrived at Bangkok port for loading.
Some ships at the port were loading around 10,000 tonnes of rice for various destinations, industry sources said.
These included 3,030 tonnes of 100 percent rice to Malaysia and 5,000 tonnes of an unknown grade to Japan.
According to the Thai Rice Mills Association, Thailand has exported 87,554 tonnes of rice between September 1-10 and 3.76 million tonnes since January 1996.
